newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PM SAYS WESTERN FEARS NOT SERIOUS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PM SAYS WESTERN FEARS NOT SERIOUS.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Thursday brushed aside western fears for democracy in Slovakia and said NATO was trying to halt Slovak efforts to be a political bridge between east and west.
Addressing a meeting of Slovak industrialists, Meciar said concerns expressed by the European Union and NATO members on the development of democracy in Slovakia were not serious.
"We do not considser these reservations to be of a principial character," Meciar said.

Slovakia's inclusion in the 16-member North Atlantic alliance as early as next year appears to have stalled following growing concern over the treatment of its minorities, in particular the 600,000-strong ethnic Hungarian community.
The U.S. State Department said on October 3 that Washington was concerned about indications that the Slovak government's commitment to democracy had been weakening.
But Meciar said there were other reasons lurking behind such statements.
"The basic demands (from NATO) are for us to give up our declaration on our wishing to be a bridge between east and west," Meciar said.
Bratislava has maintained strong ties with Moscow and has offered a possible free trade area between Russia and Slovakia.
"The second point (NATO wants) is to declare that our economic transition period has finished, accept a different economic programme, and open ourselves fully to foreign markets," he added.
He said the European Union was also pressing for Slovakia to allow foreign investors to enter domestic banks and allow foreign capital free reign in Slovakia.
"If we refuse to do this then their attitude is that there is no democracy (in Slovakia)," Meciar said.
